articleTitle: THD Mitigation in Parallel Voltage Source Converters Through Fuzzy Logic Control and SVPWM Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper aims to design and analyze the performance of parallel voltage source converters (VSCs) using space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) topology and to control the output voltage and current of the VSCs using PI and fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs). The project studies the performance of the parallel VSCs with SVPWM in terms of total harmonic distortion (THD). The proposed SVPWM technique is grounded in recent advances in fuzzy logic optimization methods, known for their suitability in solving multi-objective problems. Utilizing fuzzy logic, the technique aims to determine optimum firing angles that minimize harmonic content. The system includes parallel VSCs, RL load, LC filter and grid. The methodology entails the simulation of parallel VSCs utilizing SVPWM topology in MATLAB/Simulink, introducing FLCs into the simulation, and subsequently evaluating the parallel VSCs' performance under SVPWM topology. Additionally, the stability and robustness of the parallel VSCs, integrating both SVPWM and FLCs, are systematically analyzed. The findings reveal that employing FLCs for controlling the output voltage and current in parallel VSCs leads to a notable reduction in THD compared to conventional control methods lacking optimization methods. Comparative assessments are conducted between the performance of parallel VSCs utilizing the SVPWM technique and FLCs versus SVPWM methods without optimization technique, with a thorough analysis of stability and robustness.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of MPLS Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional Wide Area Networks (WANs) due to their ability to enhance performance and scalability. MPLS VPNs provide a secure and efficient way to connect geographically dispersed sites and offer several advantages. MPLS VPN Layer 2 and Layer 3 are two different types of MPLS-based VPNs that offer distinct advantages. In this paper we study and comparing the convergence time, packet loss, and throughput of MPLS VPN Layer 2 and Layer 3. Eve simulation and wireshark were used to acquire the results.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Method to Secure the High Embedding Capacity Steganography Based on LSB Indicator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Communicating digital information electronically is mostly insecure due to a variety of attacks. Among the data security techniques is Least Significant Bit (LSB), which used for steganography. One of drawbacks of LSB, the restriction on the amount of data transmission that effect the level of security. As result, LSB method provides lower security, when transmission high amount of data. This paper aims to increase the amount of data transmission, based on enhancement of LSB steganography technique. The data will be embedded in random bit positions of pixels to improve the security between source and destination. For testing, RGB images from Mendeley benchmark database has been used as cover images with different amount of text data. The results in this paper proved that the enhanced method, has been improv the capacity of data transmission with higher security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Semantic Communication Systems (Deep-SC) using the Pre-trained Models; BERT and BART
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In recent years, emphasis has been placed on semantic communication as one of the proposals to reach 6 generation wireless communication due to its ability to preserve basic resources for a communications network. The reason for the development in this field is the remarkable development in deep learning, which has enabled us to enable these systems. One of these proposed systems is the deep learning based semantic communication system named Deep-SC which is a system based on transformer for text transmission, which shows a great potential in sent text over physical channel in low signal-to-noise (SNR) regime. In this paper, a new system was proposed using pre-trained models in the semantic encoder and decoder. That was done by utilizing BART and BERT models instead of the transformer model. The work contributes to the ongoing effort to bridge the gap between machine and human communication by demonstrating the transformative potential of leveraging pre-trained models like BERT and BART. BLEU Score and Sentence Similarity are used as performance metrics to assess the system performance. The results showed that the proposed system has significant enhanced the system performance against benchmark systems. It has shown more robustness to channel variation and achieved better performance, especially in low SNR conditions.

articleTitle: Improving the Security and Reliability of SDN Controller REST APIs Using JSON Web Token (JWT) with OpenID and auth2.0
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: As Software-Defined Networking (SDN) continues to gain popularity, the need for secure and efficient methods of authenticating users and controlling access to network resources becomes increasingly important. RESTful APIs are commonly used in SDN to enable communication between applications and network devices through the controllers. However, without proper authentication mechanisms, these APIs can be vulnerable to attacks such as injection and unauthorized access. This paper proposes lighter and reliable REST API authentication solution with less open configuration for Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controllers based on JSON Web Token (JWT), OpenID and auth2.0. The proposed solution offers a secure and efficient way to authenticate and authorize users, control access to network resources, and protect against injection attacks. It consists of generating a secret key, defining the JWT payload, generating the JWT, including the JWT in the HTTP Authorization header, verifying the JWT, extracting the payload from the JWT, and implementing token refresh. The solution is implemented using a combination of libraries in Python [requests-json-http.client] and tested on an SDN controller using a cisco DNA sandbox network environment. The results show that the proposed authentication solution is highly efficient and effective, making it suitable for use in high-performance SDN environments. It provides a much-needed solution for securing RESTful APIs in SDN controllers, and we hope that it will encourage further research in this area.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Impact of Symmetrical Voltage Sag on the Performance of Three Phase Induction Motors-Based Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: We study the problem of symmetrical voltage sag and its effect on the characteristics of three phase induction motors (IMs) using Matlab/Simulink; we only consider symmetrical voltage sag since it is the most severe type of voltage sag. We consider three scenarios of operation: full load, partial load and no load. In each scenario, we start our investigation on symmetrical voltage sag of 50% magnitude by studying its effect on the motor torque, speed, currents, efficiency, and power factor, and then we extend our investigation on symmetrical voltage sag of different magnitudes (ranging from 90% to 10% magnitude) by studying its effect on the motor input power, currents, and speed. Our simulation results show that depending on the level of the motor loading and the magnitude of symmetrical voltage sag, the motor characteristics mentioned above may be negatively or positively affected. The findings of this study will provide a deep understanding of the behavior of three phase IMs when subjected to voltage sag and offer guidance for future research on the topic of power quality disturbances and their influence on induction machines.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Radar Cross Section Based on Parameters Affecting Surface Shape
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In the civilian world, it is frequently desirable to boost target radar detection performance, but in the military, increasing adversary radar vehicle detection performance can pose a threat. As a result, strategies to lower radar detection and raise target survivability must be researched. The radar cross section (RCS) must be decreased in order to lessen the likelihood that the targets will be picked up by the radar. The target is more likely to complete its mission successfully before it is picked up by enemy radars the lower the RCS. Examining how a target is shaped in order to achieve specific shapes that make it challenging for the radar to identify it. In this study, various basic forms that had their proportions altered were examined to determine how changing the target's size affected the effectiveness of radar detection. This paper describes the RCS analysis and simulation for complex targets such as air missile, civil aircraft and military aircraft. These targets shapes have been changed to simulate and analyze the effect on RCS and compare it with the original shape of the target that designed to complete certain missions.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation of Epsilon (Eps) Value for DBSCAN Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Cluster analysis or Clustering is considered a very important technique in the field of Data Mining. There are many approaches to clustering i.e., partitioning-based, hierarchal based and density based. In such approaches, many algorithms have been developed. One of the most common approaches in clustering algorithms is based on an examination of cluster density. Although density-based algorithms employ a variety of techniques, one of the most often referenced in the academic literature is the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm. The DBSCAN algorithm is used in a wide range of applications. This is due to the fact that this algorithm can find clusters of arbitrary shapes and sizes and its' robustness to noises which contributes a great deal to its success. However, there is a crucial problem with the correct choice of its two input parameters values, namely, the neighborhood radius (Eps) and the MinPts. The purpose of this research is to address the fundamental challenge in employing the clustering algorithm, which is to determine the input parameter (Eps) value automatically, and that by introducing a novel hybrid approach that combines the Genetic Algorithm (GA) with the DBSCAN algorithm, named GA-DBSCAN, to automatic determine the optimal value for the Eps parameter.

articleTitle: Assessing Random Power Flow for Vehicle-to-Grid Operation Based on Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper employs Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to assess how randomly power flow is distributed in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) operations. V2G technology facilitates a bidirectional flow of electricity by allowing Electric Vehicles (EVs) to feed excess power back into the grid in addition to drawing power from it. The researchers used Monte Carlo simulation as a computational technique that involves generating random samples to analyze the behaviour of a system, to assess the impact of random variations in power flow on V2G operations. They considered various factors such as EV charging and discharging patterns, grid conditions, and user behaviour to create a realistic simulation environment. The main objective function in this study wants to achieve is to reduce the dependency on the grid and develop a stochastic framework for the efficient management of microgrids with the presence of EVs. reduce cost. As a result, the analysis of the MCS shows the performance of the bidirectional operation, and the output power of the integrated sources is obtained.

articleTitle: Adoption of Blockchain Technology in the Packaged Beverage Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The distribution route for packaged drinks made from fresh food from farmers to customers involves many parties, such as processing, distribution, and sales. The authenticity and safety of the raw materials for packaged drinks, as well as supporting ingredients mixed into packaged drinks, are important for customers who enjoy drinks. The problem is that currently, the packaged beverage supply chain does not have a monitoring mechanism for the raw materials and supporting ingredients in the drinks consumed by customers. In fact, the transparency of beverage raw materials and beverage additives is important information that customers must know because these components will have an impact on customer health and safety. So the packaged beverage supply chain must have a monitoring mechanism for information on raw materials and additional ingredients for packaged drinks. Blockchain technology is a technology that has the advantage of providing transparency and information security in information systems. Thus, the aim of this research is to adopt blockchain technology in the packaged beverage supply chain. The research method uses a qualitative approach in the initial stage of identifying problems in the packaged beverage supply chain. The next stage is looking for alternative solutions using an information technology approach. The final stage is building a model and carrying out simulations with sample data using blockchain.

articleTitle: Design of 20MW Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Power Plant in Tawergha
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The primary goal in the design of a photovoltaic system is to ensure that the energy obtained from sunlight aligns with the energy needs of the load it serves. Various factors, such as environmental conditions (such as sunlight intensity and module temperature), inverter characteristics (such as operating point and minimum power requirement for grid connection), and grid integration, impact the amount of energy a grid-connected photovoltaic system can generate. System designers must have a comprehensive understanding of the parameters that affect system performance and safety, as well as those that can be adjusted without significant consequences. Factors like location, tilt, orientation, power rating, system voltage, and electrical specifications of system components are considered critical for the successful design of a photovoltaic system. This paper considers the comparison between fixed and tracking panels, as well as the comparison between string inverters and central inverters. In this paper, the possibility of utilizing suitable terrain in Libya for large-scale photovoltaic power plants connected to the national grid is explored. The paper specifically examines the design of a 20 MWp grid-connected solar PV plant in Tawergha City. The study aims to determine the optimum design that minimizes power loss and increases the generated power by varying design variables. The results show that the generated power using a tracking panel is 25% more than that used by a fixed panel, and the central inverter has higher losses compared to the string inverter. Finally, the reduction in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions was calculated. The analysis was conducted using PVsyst

articleTitle: Rooftop Solar PV System in Libya
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper investigates grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems on rooftops as a case study, implemented in Tripoli, Libya. A comprehensive survey encompassing plant design and detailed performance analysis is conducted to enhance understanding and optimize the operational behavior of PV systems installed on Libyan households' rooftops. The study examines two scenarios: a grid-connected PV system without a battery and a grid-connected PV system with a battery. The findings demonstrate the economic advantages of installing PV systems, including sufficient energy generation and surplus energy feeding into the grid during periods of excess production. Furthermore, the study highlights substantial environmental benefits, such as the avoidance of emissions equivalent to thousands of tons of CO2. The results aim to elucidate the benefits and challenges associated with increasing the penetration levels of PV systems in the Libyan electric network.

articleTitle: Solar Radiation Prediction In Libya Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In recent times, there has been a growing trend of utilizing neural networks in the field of prediction engineering, particularly in the domain of solar radiation predictions. This particular research study delves into the application of two types of neural networks, namely feedforward neural networks (BPNN) and radial basis function networks (RBFN), in the task of forecasting daily solar radiation levels across various cities in Libya. The models are trained using a comprehensive dataset from 25 cities across Libya, spanning a time period of 6 years. Key parameters such as latitude, longitude, and month are taken into consideration during the training process. Subsequently, the networks are put to the test using data that was not included in the training phase. The findings of this study reveal that the performance of the two networks differs significantly when subjected to testing. Notably, the radial basis function network emerges as the superior performer, exhibiting performance metrics of 93% compared to the backpropagation neural network's slightly lower performance of 93.15%.

articleTitle: Efficient Real-time Book Cover Text Extraction with YOLOv8 and SpaCy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the integration of advanced image processing and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract textual content from book cover images. Our approach leverages YOLOv8 for accurate text localization, Pytesseract for optical character recognition (OCR) to digitize text regions, and spaCy for deep NLP analysis, aiming to detect text comprehensively. The study is grounded in a dataset of 306 varied book cover images, meticulously compiled to train and evaluate our model's effectiveness across a spectrum of design aesthetics. The YOLOv8 model demonstrated a remarkable precision rate of 91.2

articleTitle: Real-Time Vehicles Speed Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The requirement for precise and effective ways to track the speed of vehicles has grown in the fast-paced world of today. The precision and real-time monitoring of traditional speed measurement techniques, such radar guns and speed cameras, are limited. A new path for real-time vehicles speed measurement has emerged with the development of image processing tools. Through the use of computer vision, image processing techniques can extract useful information from visual data, such as pictures or video frames. Real-time accurate speed estimation of vehicles can be achieved by analyzing their motion patterns captured by cameras using advanced algorithms. This paper presents two methods for estimating the real-time speed of vehicles using image processing techniques. The first method utilizes the Lucas-Kanade algorithm, while the second method employs the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). Both approaches aim to automatically estimate the speed of vehicles from a real time sequence captured by a stationary camera. The performance of these methods for tracking of vehicles is evaluated as well in this study.

articleTitle: Singularity Configurations Investigation of FANUC LR MATE 200ID Arm Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Singularity is a fundamental issue with robot manipulators. The presence of singularities can extremely affect the manipulator's performance. The kinematic singularities analysis is an essential stage in manipulator design. When a manipulator is approaching a singular configuration, its degrees of freedom will reduce such that there are no feasible solutions to move into this singular direction. This paper presents a method to investigate the singularity regions analytically of a 6DOF industrial robot in particular. The singularity directions in task space for robot are clearly identified using determinant of the robot's Jacobian matrix. Manipulator singularities are decoupled into the forearm and the wrist singularities. This approach is illustrated and verified experimentally on FANUC LR MATE 200ID robot arm.

articleTitle: Electron Mobility Calculations and Scattering Effects in GaN Compound Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Compound semiconductors allow processing in electronic devices much faster than silicon-based devices since electrons can travel much faster than their counterparts in silicononly devices. Electron mobility for n-GaN compound semiconductor is calculated using simulation via relaxation time at different temperatures (up to 400 K) and different doping concentrations considering four elastic scattering mechanisms; namely: neutral impurity-, ionized impurity-, piezoelectric- and acoustic phonon-scattering. It is found that electron mobility of GaN increases as temperature increases for ionized impurity scattering, but it decreases for acoustic deformation and piezoelectric scatterings; while neutral impurity scattering was not affected by temperature changes. At higher temperatures, mobility due to piezoelectric scattering approaches that of deformation scattering and can be neglected. Mobility, at low temperatures, decreases with increasing doping concentrations. At room temperature, mobility also decreases as the n-GaN becomes increasingly doped most likely explained by massive ionized impurity scattering which restricts electron mobility. The low-field mobility of electrons generally decreases when temperature increases. The obtained results are compared with that from the literature exhibiting very good agreements.

articleTitle: Sliding-Mode Controller for Collective Transport using Decentralized Multi-Robot Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The use of multi-robot systems has been increasing lately, where they are a collection of robots that work together and communicate in order to achieve their design requirement. These systems gained a significant interest in the field of robotics due to the numerous benefits they offer such as efficiency, flexibility, and robustness. One important application for these systems is collective transport, which can rise in different arrangements such as construction and assembly in space and underwater. These applications will require the development of a control strategy that is robust to uncertainties and the dynamics of the environment. In this paper a sliding mode control scheme is used to allow the system to Reach the desired values within a finite timeframe and overcome the non-linearities in the system's dynamics. Extensive simulations were conducted to prove the effectiveness of the sliding mode controller in achieving robust and effective multi-robot collective transport.

articleTitle: Effect of VGPN on Missile GNC System Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of the Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) system for air-to-air missiles using a variable navigation gain proportional navigation (VGPN) homing guidance rule. To evaluate the accuracy, stability, and responsiveness of the GNC system, the study offers a comprehensive simulation of the system. The guidance component uses the two-dimensional PN algorithm to track and target the intended item. A PID controller is utilized to offer the appropriate longitudinal acceleration commands based on the guidance input. A longitudinal state-space model is employed to link the acceleration commands from the guidance to the actual acceleration output. To increase system stability, a low-pass filter is integrated into the navigation component.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Using AutoML Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper focuses on improving human activity recognition using smartphones by training the model using H2O AutoML on a dataset called WISDM. This dataset was collected from smartphone users performing various human activities such as walking, jogging, standing, sitting, upstairs, and downstairs, and was used to train the model. The model's performance was improved using H2O AutoML and evaluated using various performance metrics such as classification accuracy and F1 score. The results showed significant improvement in the model's performance in identifying various human activities, indicating the effectiveness of using H2O AutoML to improve machine learning-based models for human activity recognition using smartphones. This model can be used in various applications such as fitness, healthcare, and smart application control. It is expected to improve users' quality of life and performance in various fields.

articleTitle: Enhancing Speech Emotion Recognition through a Cross-Dataset Analysis: Exploring Improved Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) due to its wide-ranging applications. To enhance the accuracy of emotion recognition systems, this paper employs a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM), both of which have been previously proposed and extensively studied in various research works. The ConvLSTM model adeptly captures important audio features effectively, leading to improved performance. The study includes a comprehensive analysis across multiple datasets, including RAVDESS, SAVEE, EMO-DB, and TESS, to evaluate the performance of the ConvLSTM model. Data augmentation (DA) techniques are employed to increase the training data, and feature selection using the Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) technique is utilized to identify the most informative features. The proposed approach demonstrates its effectiveness in identifying optimal configurations, which leads to high accuracy rates. Specifically, the approach achieves an accuracy of 97.16% for the the RAVDESS dataset, 97.45% for SAVEE, 97.98% for EMODB, and a perfect accuracy of 100% for TESS. Furthermore, when combining the RAVDESS, SAVEE, and EMODB datasets, the approach achieves an accuracy of 97.37% for the R+T+E dataset, and an even higher accuracy of 99.27% when combining the RA VDESS, SA VEE, and TESS datasets (R+S+T). These results underscore the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately classifying speech emotions across diverse datasets, highlighting its potential for practical applications in emotion recognition tasks.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Performance of Signalized Intersection Using Synchro Simulation Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Traffic congestion has emerged as a crucial issue in urban cities, especially at signalized intersections, causing long queues, longer travel times and environmental problems. The effectiveness of the road system is heavily dependent on the performance of signalized intersections. This research focuses on the Al-Salmani signalized intersection in Benghazi as a case study to highlight the delay and level of service (LOS) issues prevalent in Benghazi intersections. The intersection holds considerable importance within the traffic system of Benghazi due to its strategic location at the eastern entrance, adjacent to the city center. The aim of this paper is to optimize traffic operations in the Al-Salmani signalized intersection by examining three proposed scenarios including modifications in cycle length, heavy vehicle restriction and additional lane construction. Synchro 11 simulation software is used to evaluate and improve the delay and LOS at the intersection. The result of this study indicates that the intersection is operating under the unsuitable condition with LOS (F). Furthermore, Alternative scenarios 1,2, and 3 show decreases in delay values of 81.25%, 86.41%, and 92.91%. Scenario 2 showed an improvement in LOS, reaching LOS C, and scenario 3 advanced to LOS B.

articleTitle: Addressing the Libyan Arabic Dialect Identification: A Comparative Study of Ensemble Classification Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Dialect identification presents a challenging task within the realm of Natural Language Processing. The growing utilization of Arabic dialects in written form, particularly on social media platforms, has created new demands for accurate identification of these dialects. In multilingual datasets, distinguishing the Libyan Arabic dialect from neighboring Arabic dialects has emerged as a crucial goal. To address this, we conducted experiments using different lengths of word n-gram features to determine the most suitable combination of word n-grams and term frequency-inverse document frequency. Our aim was to capture contextual information effectively while mitigating linguistic similarities between Arabic dialects of neighboring countries. The QCRI Arabic Dialects Identification dataset was employed, and we evaluated the performance of three ensemble tree-based classification methods: Random Forest, Gradient Boost Machine, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting. The evaluation, based on the f-measure metric, yielded respective scores of 68%, 37%, and 52% for Random Forest, Gradient Boost Machine, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting. These results underscore the effectiveness of our approach in identifying the Libyan Arabic dialect and highlight the potential of ensemble tree-based methods in Arabic dialect identification tasks.

articleTitle: Minimizing the Viruses Propagation in Interconnected Complex Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic behavior of the spread of viruses between two interconnected subnets, R1 and R2, for two network models. For that, a new model of virus spread, based on the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) model and the minimal traffic model for a routing protocol, has been proposed. articleTitle: An Upgraded Back-stepping DC-Link Voltage Controller for On-Grid Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In order to increase the efficiency and dependability of two-stage PV grid-connected systems, this paper suggests an improvement of the voltage controller for the DC-link. This controller's primary goal is to continuously keep the DC link voltage around its reference value. This keeping smooth power transfer to the grid and improves the energy quality injected into the grid. It is proposed to improve the backstepping voltage control of the DC link via simplification of error. To assess the recommended control, three scenarios in voltage control of DC link are tested and compared, such as PI control, backstepping control, and the simplified backstepping control. The experiments for these three scenarios are conducted in MATLAB.Simulink. The final results show an improvement in the minimization of ripple phenomena, the minimization of chattering phenomena, and the minimization of total harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Efficiency Investigation of Wireless Power Transfer System for Biomedical Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In the past ten years, the wireless power transfer (WPT) systems have garnered a lot of attention, particularly in the field of the implantable medical devices. The WPT systems offer a safe and effective charging method for implant leading to reduce the cost and risks related to the surgical battery replacement. The most popular three configurations, of WPT systems, are based on two-coil, three-coil, and four-coil. Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) is considered as one of the performance indicators, as the daily activities like breathing and motion of a human being can lead to the misalignment of coils, thereby reducing the PTE. In this research paper, a finite element method (FEM), Ansys Maxwell software was used to investigate and compare the potential performance of the various designs based on two-coil, three-coil, and four-coil for spiral planar coils. The receiver coil was smaller in size potentially attaining the highest efficiency of power, and exhibiting a higher misalignment tolerant capability. In that, the alignment effect was explored through the simulation environment, where the four-coil system achieves a larger high range of efficiency and shows higher misalignment tolerant capability compared to the two-coil and three-coil system.

articleTitle: Exploring the Feasibility of Implementing a Rooftop PV System at Brega Petroleum Marketing Company and Its Economic Advantages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper is aimed at harnessing the potential of photovoltaic energy systems as a means to address the electricity production deficit and reduce fuel expenses. Photovoltaic systems (PVs) hold great promise in Libya due to its location in an area with exceptionally high solar radiation levels, averaging 2,270 KWh/m2/day annually, and approximately 3,200 hours of sunlight throughout the year. Solar energy proves to be a dependable energy source across all seasons. The primary focus of this research is the implementation of photovoltaic energy systems on the rooftop of various site owned by the Brega Petroleum Marketing Company. The rooftop area available for installation amounts to 4000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This study encompasses a thorough examination of plant design and detailed performance analysis, considering two scenarios: a grid-connected PV system (GCPV) without batteries and a grid-independent PV system with batteries. The analysis is conducted using the PV*Syst Software. Furthermore, this research delves into the economic feasibility and environmental impact of the proposed rooftop PV systems. The findings reveal that these systems generate a substantial amount of solar energy, totaling 872 MWh/year. This leads to a reduced Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) for the grid-connected system, amounting to 0.02 EURO/KWh, resulting in a significant reduction in tariff costs. Additionally, the environmental benefits are substantial, with the avoidance of the emission of thousands of tons of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Long Short-Term Memory Employed for Classifying P300-Based BCI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Designed to help patients with motor impairments such as “locked-in” syndrome, a brain-computer interface (BCI) is a device that uses brain signals for communication. This method, which focuses on neuromuscular illnesses in particular, depends on accurate and consistent detection of brain signals. In devices such as the P300 Speller, where it is used to choose desired alphabets, the P300 brain wave is essential. Because of its spatiotemporal nature, poor signal-to-noise ratio, and complexity, the P300 signal is difficult to recognize. In contrast to other options like convolutional neural networks (CNNs), this study investigates the use of long-short term memory (LSTM) as a deep learning technique for P300 signal recognition. In terms of managing and predicting spelling data, the results show that both CNN and LSTM models work well, with equivalent accuracy in P300 paradigm identification.

articleTitle: Adaptive Wavelet Techniques for Pattren Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Wavelet analysis, a computational method, decomposes data into frequency components, analyzed by scale, effective for signals with discontinuities. Originating from diverse fields like mathematics, physics, and engineering, wavelet theory finds applications in image compression, radar, and more. Using scalable wavelet functions, it allows precise signal reconstruction, differing from constant scale methods. This study compares adapted and traditional wavelets, emphasizing Finite Impulse Response (FIR) efficiency. Applying these wavelets for pattern recognition, particularly in spike detection in EEG data, highlights their versatility in complex signal processing.

articleTitle: An Improved Genetic Algorithm Tool for Exam Timetabling Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The timetabling problem is a well-known challenge in education management. It involves scheduling various events, such as classes, exams, and meetings, within limited time and resources. It requires carefully balancing numerous constraints and preferences, such as room availability, faculty availability, and student preferences. This problem is known as Non-deterministic Polynomial (NP). This paper used a new genetic algorithm, including encoded and fitness function techniques, to solve the faculty exam timetable problem. The tool's results were positive compared to similar findings from other studies. The outcomes also show how quickly the tool can produce more tables.

articleTitle: Control the Interval Estimation to Enhance the Performance of Optimized Link State Routing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper investigates the creation of self-organizing Mobile Ad hoc Networks (MANETs) employing Optimized Link State Routing Protocol (OLSR) with Multipoint Relay (MPR). The routing protocol in MANET controls the management of node mobility by using metrics to evaluate the quality of link states. The primary concept of OLSR is to choose the MPR that identifies the route from the source to the destination node. The MPR relays Hello and Topology Control (TC) messages between nodes used to discover and distribute link state information. The Hello and TC messages interval plays a critical role in the link state in the network. Accordingly, link failure for a few seconds may lead to a significant performance deterioration. This work enhances the performance of OLSR by estimating the efficient Hello and TC message interval for faster route recovery. Many experiments are simulated and analyzed by a set of parameters such as MPR count, TC traffic sent, throughput, delay, and data dropped. All our results revealed that the proposed Control of the Interval Estimation-Optimized Link State Routing (CIE-OLSR) has better performance than the traditional OLSR.

articleTitle: Modified Asymmetric 25-Level H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The multilevel inverter (MLI) is a significant application for converting direct current to alternating current. This is due to the growing demand for renewable energy sources that provide direct current. Recently, researchers have focused on reducing the cost of MLI by reducing the number of inverter components. This paper proposes a Modified Asymmetric 25-level H-bridge Multilevel Inverter (MA25-MLI) with only 9 switches and 3 voltage sources, as opposed to the 48 switches and 12 voltage sources used in conventional Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverters (CHB-MLI), which contributes to cost, weight, and loss reduction. The inverter was controlled using the Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) technology. MATLAB Simulink was used to build and run the suggested inverter, and the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD%) of the output voltage was computed and compared to earlier studies.

articleTitle: Improving Facial Expression Recognition in HCI: Traditional Techniques and Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Facial expressions play a vital role in human communication, enabling us to convey a wide range of emotions such as happiness, anger, and sadness. Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a rapidly growing and highly appealing field. By recognizing facial expressions, HCI can enhance communication by making it more interactive and natural. The proposed methodology is based on traditional techniques for extracting and classifying the features from images. To evaluate its effectiveness, we utilize two datasets: CK+ and JAFFE. First, the facial part of the images is cropped and enhanced using a CLAHE filter. Then, the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) descriptor extracts features from the images, while Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduces their dimensionality. Finally, three classifiers Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Random Forest are used to classify facial expressions. Our methodology achieved an accuracy of 95.94% for CK+ and 93.75% for JAFFE datasets.

articleTitle: Simulating Photovoltaic Emulator Systems for Renewable Energy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The article discusses exploring the Photovoltaic (PV) emulator for simulating photovoltaic systems for Renewable Energy Analysis (REA) focuses on creating and applying a PV emulator to simulate photovoltaic systems and concludes by emphasizing the value of precise simulation tools in comprehending and enhancing photovoltaic system performance. The first portion of the article emphasizes how renewable energy sources especially solar energy are becoming more and more important in tackling the world's energy problems. As a result, the pv output along with the voltage and current have been presented

articleTitle: Digital Image Encryption Based On Elliptic Curve Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Information security is currently a major problem for data communication. Cryptography has emerged as a treatment and is essential to information security systems. Techniques for encryption can effectively prevent attacks on images. Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is an approach of public-key encryption, depends on the algebraic grouping of elliptic curves over finite fields. The present study introduces an intriguing elliptic curve cryptography-based image encryption approach and applied it to various images. The proposed technique was tested. We computed the number of pixels change rate (NPCR), unified average changing intensity (UACI), and peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) to assess the effectiveness of the suggested technique.

articleTitle: Detecting Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease using Brain Signals: An EEG Based Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a long-term illness character-ized by a decline in abilities and the development of dementia. The main objective of this study is to explore the potential of using EEG-based classification for identifying and comprehending Alzheimer's disease in its stages. EEG, which measures brain ac-tivity, offers insights into the functioning of neurons. By applying machine learning techniques to EEG data, we have seen results in distinguishing between individuals with Alzheimer's disease and those without it. For our research, we used a dataset that included EEG recordings from individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy individuals for comparison. We extracted Mel coefficients (MFCC) as features and trained our models using decision trees and LightGBM classifiers. To evaluate their effectiveness, we assessed accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the operating curve (AUC ROC). Our results showed accuracy in differentiating between Alzheimer's patients and healthy individuals, with an 89.3% accuracy rate along with AUC ROC values of 0.989 for the decision tree classifier and 98.64 % and 1.0 for the Igbm classifier, respectively. These findings highlight the potential of combining EEG-based classification with machine learning algorithms for diagnosis and personalized treatment planning for Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Mesh Wire at Low Frequencies in Near Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Electronic circuits are used widely today for a variety of purposes, including computing, automation, and communication. Additionally, the size of electronic devices has decreased due to the widespread use of integrated circuits and integration. As electronic devices shrink and pack more circuits into tighter spaces, their proximity can lead to unwanted interference. This “electromagnetic interference” (EMI) is a growing concern for designers, not only for functionality but also for potential health risks. Electromagnetic shielding is the process of minimizing electromagnetic field penetration into space by blocking them with a conductive barrier. This study investigated the effectiveness of wire mesh as an EMI shield. Using the simulations program (CST STUDIO SUITE), a circular antenna was placed at the center, and a wire mesh barrier was positioned at various distances. The strength of the electromagnetic field was measured both with and without the shielding, across a range of frequencies and for various mesh configurations (dimensions and material). The results demonstrated the potential of wire mesh for EMI shielding. With specific combinations of mesh dimensions and materials, a shielding efficiency of about 20 dB was achieved in the range of 500 to 1500 Hz, particularly at 1000 Hz. This demonstrates the potential of wire mesh as an EMI mitigation option in a range of applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implement a PC-Based SCADA Education System, Part I: Power System Load Frequency Control and Governor Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: PC-Based control has many advantages over other control systems like Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) base or Programmable Automation Controller (PAC) base control system, such as updating to handle more data processing by simply adding processing power or extend the memory that allows running and processing third party program on the same station. This paper describes the effective, robust, and low-cost design & implementation of a PC-based SCADA education system for the centralized control automatic generation control (AGC) of power system generators in the laboratory at the College of Electrical & Electronic Technology, Benghazi within higher graduate studies program, in this proposed system, it does not only allow the researchers to capture the raw data of the system easily but also it can be run an integrate a third party program OPC-DA for secure communications or OPC-UA for cloud connectivity. In this article, the frequency bias method is used to control power system frequency composed of two generation units using only one controller and evaluate the performance of the whole control system for multi-cases when the sleep time of the controller is changed. Profinet communication was established between the master terminal unit (MTU) and the remote terminal unit (RTU), through fiber optics cables and Small Form-factor Pluggable (SFC) Transceivers to eliminate the delay due to the communication as possible and interference immune. In this article experimental tests have been held on a simple power system 3-phase 380V, 50Hz, composed of two synchronous generator units rated 1.0 kVA each, medium transmission line model, 3-phase 450w resistive load and 1.0 hp, 3-phase induction motor with variable load represents the inductive variable load, the results obtained from the experimental tests were promising and positive, from many cases of different sleep time selected there is no effect on the whole control system performance.

articleTitle: EEG Motor Imagery Classification using Graphical Neural Networks with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This research study presents a novel approach for decoding brain activity measured by electroencephalogram (EEG) signals in brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. Traditional methods overlook the topological relationship among electrodes, which is crucial for understanding brain dynamics. To address this, we propose a deep learning framework based on graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) with an attention mechanism, aiming to enhance the decoding performance of raw EEG signals during motor imagery tasks. Our approach constructs a GCNs-Net by utilizing graph convolutional layers to learn generalized features from EEG data, considering the functional topological relationship of electrodes. Pooling layers are employed for dimensionality reduction, and a fully-connected softmax layer generates final predictions. The evaluation results demonstrate that our approach achieves a high averaged accu-racy of 95% for group levels, showing adaptability and robustness to individual variability. Moreover, the results are reproducible across multiple experiments for cross-validation, highlighting the potential of our method in improving BCI approaches.

articleTitle: Practical Evaluation of Overcurrent Protective Relay Performance in Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Power distribution system suffers several disturbances during its operation which cause problems in reliability of system. The reliability depends on the successful operation of protective relays that are used in protective scheme to detect disturbances and faults, thus reduce their effects by separating the faulty area from healthy one. In distribution system, overcurrent relays mainly are used. The failure of relay operation may cause damage of system components. The presence of overcurrent relays in distribution system has created the challenge of testing of these devices for evaluating of their performance. This paper presents practical evaluation of overcurrent protective relays performance using advanced test system (CMC test system). Advanced test system includes software that will be used for evaluating and performance analysis of overcurrent relay according to operating characteristics and relay settings. The process requires the review of work principle of overcurrent relays that were used to investigate the settings of relay in order to create test cases will confirm that the relay performance responds as expected or not.

articleTitle: Comparison of Network's Performance by Applying Integrated Services and Differentiated Services Quality of Service Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In this paper different quality of service (QoS) models were applied to compare their improvement to the performance of the network. Integrated services and differentiated services QoS models were implemented in three scenarios of a simulated network. Then parameters related to the operation of the network like, jitter, latency, and packet loss were calculated. The comparison conducted has shown that the differentiated services model has had a significant effect on improving the network's performance by reducing latency to 92 msec and jitter to 0.75 msec.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Control Parameters on the Performance of the Harmony Search Algorithm by Parametric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA) belongs to the category of metaheuristic optimization methods and has been widely utilized for various optimization problems. Since its proposal, numerous studies have been conducted to enhance its performance by refining one or more of its control parameters. The objective of this study is to investigate the influence of these control parameters on the algorithm's performance. Initially, we identify the commonly used values for the HAS's control parameters including (Harmony Memory Size HMS, Harmony Memory Consideration Rate HMCR, Pitch Adjusting Rate PAR, Bandwidth BW, and the Number of Iterations ITR). Subsequently, we employ the “one at a time” (OAT) design of the experiment technique to generate a dataset. We then utilize Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to determine which control parameter has a significant impact on the algorithm's performance. Our findings reveal that the harmony memory size (HMS) and the number of iterations (ITR) had a clear and continued impact on the performance of the algorithm throughout the entire process. While, the remaining three parameters influenced the performance of the algorithm only during the early stage of the process, Afterwards, the performance remained constant, despite their changes. These results can assist researchers and practitioners in improving the algorithm's performance by selecting appropriate values for the control parameters and focusing on fine-tuning the influential parameters rather than those with less impact.

articleTitle: Multiband PIFA Antenna Design with Optimized Defected Ground Plane Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The conception of a novel antenna design approaches has become necessary since antennas will be coupled with other components at the same terminal. The area dedicated to antennas is shrinking as the mobile phone industry advances, necessitating the development of miniature, high-performance antennas. Hence, the introduce of a binary genetic algorithm coupled with a defected ground plane to formulate a triple PIFA antenna tailored for mobile communications is analysed. This antenna is specifically designed to cover LTE Band 11, middle and upper band WiMAX, HIPERLAN/2 and WLAN. The antenna ground plane shape is defined using the evolutionary algorithm in order to provide sufficient performance for triple-band operation. The simulation results show that resonance is exhibited by the proposed antenna at three different frequencies. With a resonance frequency at 1.42 GHz, the lower bandwidth extends from 1.41 to 1.45 GHz. With corresponding ranges of 3.3 to 3.51 GHz and 4.6 to 5.8 GHz, the middle and upper bandwidths are centered at 3.41 GHz and 5.43 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: The Influence of Abrupt Symmetrical Voltage Sag on the Characteristics of Doubly Fed Induction Generator-Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIGs) are extensively employed in wind turbines due to their significant characteristics, such as the capability to supply useful power at changeable speeds, over other types of generators like synchronous generators. However, these characteristics are sensitive to voltage sag event. Therefore, in this paper, we deeply investigate the impact of abrupt symmetrical voltage sag on DFIG performance using Matlab/ Simulink. In this work, a comparison has been made between the operation of DFIG under normal condition, abrupt symmetrical voltage sag, and crowbar protection circuit. Simulation results show that the abrupt symmetrical voltage sag causes adverse impacts on DFIG characteristics, and show that the existence of crowbar circuit within DFIG based wind turbine system significantly mitigates these negative effects.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Semi-Empirical Model for Controlling Radiation Sterilization Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The authors of this report, in their previous work, based on fundamental assumptions, developed an improved semi-empirical model (ISE-model) of the depth-dose (DD) distribution in the layer for the case of an arbitrary angle of incidence of the electron beam. In this report presents the stages of determining the optimal electron beam parameters for two-sided radiation sterilization processes, which are calculated on the basis of an ISE-model. An algorithm has been developed for calculating the parameter of an ISE-model, which is carried out based on a comparison of data obtained by the Monte Carlo method in a detailed physical model and using an ISE-model. Software has been created to control optimal two-sided irradiation modes and determine errors in planning these modes using ISE-model of the sterilization process. Methods are given for taking into account the electrons spectrum when calculating the optimal angles of incidence of the beam on the surface of the product and assessing the uncertainty of realizing the maximum efficiency of the yield of the irradiated product.

articleTitle: A New Topology of Multi-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: According to the spread of Multi-Level Inverter (MLI) in the high power and medium voltage applications and their advantages but at the cost of large number of components which also makes the system more complex. Complexity increases with the increment of output voltage levels. This paper proposes a new topology of MLIs under the name of Zigzag Multilevel Inverter “ZMLI” that can generate levels 7,15,31,63 … Etc. Along with an explanation of its general circuit configuration, operating concept, and the equations that it is based on to design. Also taken a 15 and 31-Level ZMLI as examples. The performance and operation of proposed inverter is verified through simulation results through MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Flexible Wideband Microwave Absorbers with Frequency Selective Surface Based on Mechanically Treated Foiled Polymer Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The aim of the study was to experimentally substantiate the proposed by us technology for manufacturing flexible wideband microwave absorbers with frequency- selective surface containing circular patches formed from the foiled polymer film containing aluminum oxide. It was established that the effective absorption band of the samples, on the surface of which there are 3.0 cm patches formed from the smooth foiled polymer film, is 10.0-13.0 GHz. The effective absorption band of the samples, on the surface of which there are 6.0 cm and 9.0 cm patches formed from the smooth foiled polymer film, are respectively 10.5-17.0 GHz and 2.0-9.5 GHz, 10.5-12.0 GHz, 13.5-14.5 GHz, 15.5-16.5 GHz. The effective absorption band of the samples on the surface of which there are 9.0 cm circular patches, formed from the mechanically treated foiled polymer film, the average size of roughness of which is 20.0 is 9.0-11.5 GHz. The effective absorption bands of the samples, the surface of which contains 9.0 cm patches, formed from the mechanically treated foiled polymer film, the average size of roughness of which is 50.0 and 80.0 are respectively 6.0-13.5 GHz and 5.5-17.0 GHz. Thus, the absorbers manufactured in accordance with the proposed technology mechanically treated foiled polymer film, the average size of roughness of which is more than 50.0 are wideband ones. These absorbers could be used to protect radioelectronic equipment and antennas systems from microwave interferences.

articleTitle: Evaluation of BER, Reliability and Throughput During the Vertical Coexistence of 4G LTE and 5G NR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The evolution of spectrum sharing by both 4G Long Term Evolution (LTE) and 5G New Radio( NR) is what's happening in the future. The interference issues arising from this homogeneous spectrum can be reduced by employing cognitive process. Therefore Dynamic Spectrum Sharing(DSS) may be an appropriate solution. As interference issue, in general, creates difficulties in different directions for further achievements, it can cause the decline of reliability of communication, as discussed in this paper. The issue of interference, which presents difficulties for a number of further advancements. The issue of interference causes the decline of reliability of the signal. The effect of interference will vary when the oscillator power for 5G NR is variable varied while the oscillator power for 4G LTE is kept constant. According to the investigation, the signal's dependability vanishes when both 4G LTE and 5G NR have equal or nearly equal oscillator power. In this stage, the Bit Error Rate (BER) is highest and throughput becomes negligible. Hence we say that there is no reliability of the signal. To increase the reliability and throughput, the oscillator power for 5G NR must be decreased. The experimental results show that with the decrease in oscillator power for 5G NR, there will be increase in reliability and throughput of the signal.

articleTitle: Development of a Decentralized Application for Managing Food Supply Chain Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The olive oil sector in Tunisia, although prosperous, faces major challenges such as counterfeiting and irregular product quality. This paper proposes the development of a decentralised application based on blockchain technology to guarantee the traceability of Tunisian oil throughout the supply chain. Blockchain offers an innovative solution by ensuring transparency, data immutability and decentralisation, thus eliminating problems of trust and verification. This key concept will guide our design and development approach, aiming to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, minimise risk risks, and provide a rewarding experience for all elements involved. The envisaged application will not only help to build confidence within the supply chain, but will also help to enhance the value of Tunisian olive oil on national and international markets.

articleTitle: Control Technique of MPPT Utilizing for Boost Converter Applied to Small Renewable Energy System and a DC Microgrid for Remote Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The growing concerns about the environment, depletion of fossil fuels, and increasing energy consumption have led to a rise in the adoption of renewable energy sources. However, integrating these green energy sources into the existing power system requires infrastructure modifications. One popular approach is the establishment of off-grid operations through the use of microgrids. Microgrids are small-scale power systems that can operate both connected to and disconnected from the main power grid. This study focuses on a DC microgrid that utilizes a renewable energy system to power DC loads in case of a conventional grid failure. The system incorporates various components such as a universal diode rectifier, a boost converter, a small wind turbine (SWT) connected to a permanent magnet synchronous generator, and the Incremental Conductance (IC) algorithm. These components are employed to maximize the output power of the boost converter and maintain precise control over the output voltage, ensuring reliability. To efficiently operate the switching element and achieve a fast Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique and voltage regulation despite varying wind speeds, a modified IC MPPT control method is utilized. A MATLAB/Simulink model representing an SWT system for a DC microgrid is developed to assess the dependability of the proposed system under changing wind speeds.

Author Keywords: a renewable energy source of small wind turbine

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Supression Techniques Used for compact 5G MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: a compact MIMO antenna is designed to work at 28GHz and used for 5G applications. In this paper, different isolation techniques were designed and simulated to reduce the effect of the mutual such as coupling defected ground structure (DGS), slab parasitic element place on the top of the substrate between the radiating elements and electromagnetic bandgap structure (EBGs) that works as stop band filter to null out the effect of surface waves. The antenna is physically compacted to small dimensions of 10.235x 9.0187x1.149 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In this paper the concentration is mainly about the performance of decoupling techniques to remove the effect of mutual coupling (MC) for closer radiating antenna elements, where they exhibit about 5dB as a minimum difference between the evaluation of mutual coupling without and with the use of suppression decoupling techniques. The MC is reduced from 13dB to 18 dB and 20 dB. In this paper the envelop correlation coefficient (ECC), Diversity gain (DG) are also evaluated and results in less than 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> for ECC, and 10 for DG, which are more suitable for the design.

articleTitle: Classification of Cervical Cancer using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is the most common type of cancer in women. It is curable if detected early, but it is nevertheless a major cause of death, particularly in underdeveloped nations. The purpose of this study was to find efficient deep learning-based classification models for the early identification of cancer. For data classification, convolutional neural networks (CNN) are employed. We received 4049 carefully cropped photos of isolated cells from 966 images of cluster cells on Pap smear slides are available in the SIPaKMeD Database. These photos were taken with a Charged-coupled device (CCD) camera modified for use with an optical microscope. The five categories into which the cell pictures are divided include normal, aberrant, and benign cells. The classification method known as principal component analysis (PCA) was evaluated. The classification accuracy with the biopsy data was 94.198%.

articleTitle: Parallel Decoder of Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Polar codes, a recent discovery in coding theory, represent a groundbreaking family of capacity-achieving codes. They stand out as the first codes to achieve capacity for any binary discrete memoryless channel (B-DMC), constructed through the innovative channel polarization concept. Building upon the advancements in polar code techniques, this paper introduces a high-speed decoder rooted in the successive cancellation (SC) decoding framework. The focus here is on presenting the core concepts and techniques behind channel polarization, polar codes, and the high-speed decoding algorithm, enabling the parallel decoding of N bits simultaneously. The implementation of polar codes over binary erasure channels (BEC) is demonstrated, and their bit error rates are calculated at varying erasure probabilities. Through simulation results, we showcase the performance of polar codes when subjected to high-speed decoding.

articleTitle: Blockchain and IoT Technology Adoption Model for Improved Elderly Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Supervision using a real-time system to find out the health conditions of the elderly is very important. The health conditions of the elderly, which naturally continue to decline with age, require greater supervision than those of young people. Monitoring the health conditions of seniors is important for families, doctors, and health insurance. For families, monitoring the health of seniors is proof of love as a form of family relationship. For doctors, monitoring the health of the elderly is important to provide action to maintain the health of the elderly. For insurance companies, health monitoring plays an important role, especially when seniors submit insurance claims. Currently, there is no system that helps monitor elderly health by providing transparent information with a high level of security for the three parties mentioned above. So the problem statement from this research is that it is difficult to obtain transparent and guaranteed security information related to monitoring the health of the elderly. Thus, this research aims to help monitor the health of seniors using blockchain technology and the Internet of Things. The research method uses a qualitative approach by studying conventional elderly health monitoring mechanisms, blockchain technology mechanisms, and internet of things technology. The result of this research is a blockchain and IoT adoption model for monitoring elderly health. The research results are complemented by transaction simulations related to monitoring elderly health.

articleTitle: On Demand User Association and Load Distribution with Guaranteed Rate in Multi UAV-Assisted Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The recent advent of emergent networks (5G and 6G) has led to an exponential growth in the number of smart devices in circulation. Deployment of a group of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV s) to a site to satisfy customers' minimal QoS demands is one way to meet the ever-increasing need for network coverage. The main challenge that we address in this paper is how to placement these UAV s such that the load is fairly distributed among the UAVs, and the data rate per customer is maximized. Both consumers and providers have a stake in solving this issue. As for consumers, better and more predictable QoS of the networks makes for a better experience. And for providers, happier customers mean more revenue and longer customer retention. In this work, we propose a heuristic algorithm to compute the placement of the UAVs taking into account the locations of the users, their minimum QoS capacities, and the UAV service capacities. Empirical results show that our approach is superior to a planned server network in terms number of served users and fairness among base stations.

articleTitle: Iron Deficiency Diagnosis Using Combined FMM-based Features and SVM on Lemon Leaf Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Diagnosing iron deficiency in the lemon plant is one of the early ways to prevent and preserve the plant. Diagnosis of iron deficiency depends on the emergence of green veins in young lemon leaves (buds) as a result of a decrease in the leaf color of the plant (yellow leaf). In this research, it was proposed to use the technique of the Fuzzy Mathematical Morphology FMM and Histogram to extract the features of young lemon leaf images using a database collected from the Botanical Department, Faculty of Science, Misurata University. This database consisted of 210 images that were divided into three categories: leaves with iron deficiency, healthy leaves, and leaves with other diseases. These FFM-based extracted database features were classified using the Support Vector Machine SVM classifier, where 70% of the dataset features were used for training, and 30% for testing. The system's performance was further enhanced by incorporating the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) with the FMM-based features. Evaluations showed significant improvement: FMM alone achieved 83% accuracy, FMM with histogram analysis reached 95%, and the combined FMM/Histogram/GLCM approach reached the highest accuracy of 97%.

articleTitle: Airline Scheduling Model Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Airline scheduling, the backbone of airline expansion and survival, faces a monumental challenge: finding the opti-mal flight schedule among countless possibilities under numerous constraints. This nondeterministic polynomial time (NP problem) demands innovative solutions. This paper proposes a genetic algorithm approach to build feasible daily schedules and assign optimal aircraft for hub-and-spoke airlines. The model delivers near-optimal solutions suitable for practical implementation, demonstrating the effectiveness of the genetic approach.

articleTitle: Empowering Remote Regions: Modelling and Simulation of a 1.54 MW Off-Grid Fuel-Cell Unit for Sustainable Energy Independence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This article provides an analysis of a 1.54 MW off-grid fuel cell system designed to empower remote populations and attain sustainable energy autonomy. Amidst a time when the availability of electricity is still a significant worry in isolated regions, the focus on off-grid solutions is increasing. The study employs Simulink to examine the dynamics of the off-grid fuel cell system. The mathematical models of the different entities such as the fuel cell stack, three-phase neutral clamped point inverter, the LCL filter and the control parameters, all involved in the systems are established first to determine the components' characteristics, then all these entities are integrated as a single system under the Simulink tool to assess the off-grid system response. The findings show that the system can deliver an active power of 1.4 MW at a voltage of 600 V between phases, and maintain the total harmonic distortion below 5% to provide power to the remote region provided that hydrogen is supplied at the input of the fuel cell stack. The results also revealed that the designed off-grid system can achieve an efficiency of 90 %.
