The simulation aimed to test two scenarios: one where the classical PID controller was tuned using a trial-and-error method, and the other where the Genetic PID controller was employed to tune the PID parameters. The study's main objective was to understand how the system behaved under various input types and different values. Additionally, a comparison between the two control design approaches was presented. The control design methods employed in this study hold the promise of achieving optimal control over the robotic arm while improving response and stability. Finally, simulations were conducted, and the results were compared for both cases. A comprehensive conclusion was drawn based on the findings of the study.

articleTitle: An Effect of Huffman Encoding with Hybrid Edge Detection in LSB Image Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: With the development and spread of technology in the world and its increasing speed, the danger of attacking data has increased and spread with it, therefore, data exchanged between the parties must be protected from hackers and kept confidential. The art of concealing digital data so that no one can surmise its existence is known as steganography. Steganography is used to hide the existence of such data by enclosing the secret in a cover image, creating a new image that is nearly identical to the original. As a result, hidden data within the cover image is shielded from unwanted access. In this study, we suggested a way to hide a greyscale image on the edges of another RGB color image by using a hybrid edge detector between canny and Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG) and applying it to the cover image by OR operation, then dilation on those edges, then compression of the secret image by using Huffman lossless encoding and embedding these secret compressed data in the edges discovered for the cover image by least significant bit (LSB) algorithm. We demonstrated how hiding in the edge area could maintain the Stego image's quality. with good values of PSNR and MSE. Our best results achieved for MSE, PSNR, and SSIM are 0.0526, 60.9207, and 1 respectively. Our algorithm additionally shown that the secret image was correctly and distortion-free retrieved.

articleTitle: Securing Democracy: Implementing a Blockchain-Based E-Voting System in Libya
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The local election system is based on traditional paper methods, which poses various risks to the security and integrity of the electoral process. In an effort to address these challenges and improve the accuracy and transparency of elections in Libya, this paper proposes the implementation of a blockchain-based e-voting system. Leveraging blockchain's decentralized nature, cryptographic foundations, and transparency, the proposed system aims to replace the paper-based method and provide a secure and transparent solution that ensures the integrity and tamper-proof platform of the election process. Additionally, the implementation of a proof-of-work consensus algorithm will ensure that the system is decentralized and operates in a transparent manner, ensuring the accuracy and security of the election results. This paper will provide a viable solution to the existing challenges in the Libyan election system and support the country's journey towards a more secure, transparent, and democratic future.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting with Power Splitting Scheme in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The primary component of the Internet of Things (IoT) is the Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). These networks are responsible for gathering data from the environment and transmitting it wirelessly through communication channels to the sink nodes. Wireless Sensor Nodes are typically deployed in hard-to-reach locations with limited power sources. As a result, researchers have sought out innovative approaches such as energy harvesting (EH) and power splitting (PS) to enhance energy efficiency and prolong the lifespan of wireless networks. Radio frequency (RF) is a readily available and cost-free energy source that can be harnessed to generate the desired voltage. This energy can be harvested from the surrounding environment, making it an attractive option for powering wireless sensor nodes. When more and more nodes involved in wireless sensor networks, the PS becomes crucial and it has to be efficient in such a way that every node will get the same amount of power regardless its location. This becomes a challenge to most of the PS designers for the WSN. The research adopts a power splitting scheme at the intermediate relay nodes, wherein the energy harvesting (EH) node divides the input RF signal into two parts. One part is used for energy harvesting, while the other part is utilized for information transmission. The main objective of this research is to propose a suitable power splitting (PS) scheme that incorporates radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting. This scheme aims to effectively conserve energy and enhance the energy efficiency in wireless Internet of Things (IoT) nodes. The analyzation of the proposal PS scheme will be carried out using MATLAB toolkit.

articleTitle: Technology Learning Attitudes in a Libyan Technical Higher Institute: A Technology Acceptance Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Information Technology for education is still in the adoption and implementation phases. This research aims to comprehend the several variables that affect the acceptance of technology adoption. This study examines the perception of the management, academic staff, and students toward the acceptance of technology at Alshomokh Technical Higher Institute in Libya within the framework of the Technology Acceptance Model. It was discovered that the Technology Acceptance Model is suitable for evaluating technological adoption. The Technology Acceptance Model has a Cronbach's alpha of 0.864 for ease of use, indicating a high degree of acceptance of technology use.

articleTitle: Utilizing Eeg Signals for Epilepsy Seizure Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Epilepsy is a central nervous system disease causing abnormal brain activity, odd behavior, and coma. It affects individuals of various ages and ethnicities, making seizure detection challenging due to differences in actions and brain signals. The rise in global infections has spurred the development of accurate techniques for early detection and improved treatment outcomes. The suggested method consists of three parts: preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification. Kid-specific EEG recordings from the CHB-MIT database are preprocessed to obtain a pure signal. Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) are then extracted as features. Categorization methods like Random Forest (RF) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) are utilized for classification. Study findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning algorithms in enhancing epilepsy diagnosis using EEG data. KNN achieves up to 99.05% accuracy, while Random Forest achieves 95.02% accuracy in detecting epileptic activity. These results highlight the value of machine learning in epilepsy as diagnostic and therapeutic tools.

articleTitle: Cyber Risk Management of Third-Party Relationships: The Need for an Assessment Guidelines to Regulate Private Sectors in Libya
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: the increasing reliance on third-party relationships for various services and operations, the need for an effective cyber risk management guidelines and practices becomes crucial. This paper emphasizes the necessity of assessment guidelines specifically tailored to the private sectors in Libya, outlining the steps and criteria for assessing the cyber risk of third-party relationships. By implementing these assessment guidelines, Libya can strengthen its cyber risk management practices, protect sensitive information, and mitigate potential cyber threats in the private sectors.

articleTitle: Optimizing Critical Communication Systems for Offshore Oil and Gas Operations via Computational Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The deployment of mission-critical communication systems on offshore oil and gas platforms is paramount due to the extreme and isolated environments these platforms operate in. These systems are not only crucial for ensuring the safety of personnel amid common hazards such as fires, explosions, and severe weather conditions, but they also enhance operational efficiency, environmental protection, and regulatory compliance. This paper examines the integral role of reliable and efficient communication technologies, which are essential for real-time coordination of drilling, production, and emergency response activities. Additionally, the paper discusses various offshore drilling rigs and the necessary communication infrastructures such as TErrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA), Project 25 (P25), and Digital Mobile Radio (DMR), which support diverse operational needs from machine-to-machine, human-to-machine, and human-to-human interactions. This comprehensive analysis highlights the advancements in communication technology that are critical to managing the complexities of offshore operations, ensuring continuous safety measures, and supporting the remote management of these floating industrial facilities. Finally, the paper outlines the design considerations for implementing a robust communication system tailored to the unique demands of offshore environments, including system specifications and numerical methods like the Monte Carlo and Transmission Line Matrix methods used in simulation studies to optimize communication coverage and reliability on rigs.

articleTitle: Dominance of Neural Networks in Additive Manufacturing Surface Roughness Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This article examines the prediction of surface roughness control in additive manufacturing by comparing Linear Regression and Neural Network models. Through K-means clustering, we identify four clusters in the data, each associated with specific 3D printing parameters. Within each cluster, we analyze the factors influencing surface roughness and power efficiency. The primary objective is to forecast a target variable, considering metrics such as R-squared, Mean Squared Error, and correlation coefficient. Our research demonstrates that both Linear Regression and Neural Network models exhibit strong predictive capabilities, with the Neural Network outperforming the Linear Regression model. The Neural Network demonstrates superior performance metrics, reduced Mean Squared Error, and greater resilience to outliers. These results underscore the effectiveness of Neural Networks in achieving precision and identifying nonlinear patterns in surface roughness prediction. Thus, emphasizing the significance of employing advanced machine learning techniques, such as Neural Networks, in similar domains.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Architectures for RSSI Based Indoor Localization using Trilateration Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The common lateration method estimates the position of an unknown target by using the positions of reference nodes and the RSSI values that reflect the distances between the target and the reference nodes. However, the variability of RSSI signals in the physical environment, influenced by factors such as time-varying conditions and multipath effects, is a significant contributor to localization errors. These inaccuracies can adversely affect system decisions. In challenging environments, Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) operate, making maintenance and battery replacement difficult tasks. Optimizing node deployment techniques becomes critical to strategically position nodes for optimal coverage, improve accuracy, and conserve network activity to extend its lifetime. This paper presents a comparative analysis of three architectures to evaluate the accuracy and longevity of wake-up receiver sensor node deployment. Specifically, the application focuses on indoor localization of anchors using trilateration and RSSI measurements in the context of rectangular grid structures with two types of map segmentation and hexagonal grid architecture.

articleTitle: AI-Based QoS Optimization in Post-Disaster Ad Hoc Networks: Top-K Path Enumeration with Multicriteria Decision Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper presents the Topkws algorithm, an efficient method for enumerating the k shortest paths in an Ad hoc network. The algorithm is specifically designed for disaster management scenarios, such as earthquakes, and utilizes top-k ranking from nodes. The approach is based on the Topkws recommendation algorithm, which incorporates Machine Learning (ML) techniques. These ML techniques are used for AI-driven recommendation, enhancing the algorithm's ability to handle complex network scenarios. It employs Multicriteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with a weighted sum method to order paths based on Quality of Service (QoS) attributes like hop count, bandwidth, delay, and cost. By optimizing QoS characteristics, the algorithm effectively reduces traffic in the network, thereby improving overall performance. The research demonstrates the importance of efficiently obtaining the necessary data elements in an ad hoc network using top-k issues, thereby ensuring the optimal use of resources in post-disaster scenarios.

articleTitle: The Impact of Trust, Perceived Credibility, and Perceived Self-Efficacy on The Acceptance of Mobile Banking in Libya
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The use of smartphone technology has been advantageous for both customers and banks. Nevertheless, the adoption rate of Mobile Banking tools in Libya, specifically in the city of Tarhana, remains low. The study aims investigate the acceptance of Mobile Banking in Libya by employing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Data was gathered through a survey of M-Banking customers from August to December 2023, with 359 respondents participating in an online questionnaire in Tarhuna city. The data was then analyzed using AMOS v21 and SPSS v28. The findings reveal that both the ease of use and usefulness of the M-Banking application in use in Libya banks were affected by self-efficacy, trust, and perceived credibility. This suggests that users in Libya have confidence in their ability to use the app and trust its credibility. However, users do not perceive it as useful or user-friendly. Future research could explore the indirect influence between customers attitudes towards usage and self-efficacy, trust, and perceived credibility, particularly in traditional banks located in Tripoli.

articleTitle: Customer Churn Prediction Using Machine Learning: A Case Study of Libyan Internet Service Provider Company
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a field of science and technology that simulates human intelligence to develop intelligent machines. Machine Learning (ML), on the other hand, is a subset of AI that enables computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. In the area of business, data science is the practical application of ML, AI, and statistics, which focuses on extracting valuable insights from data. Nowadays, data science relies heavily on ML techniques, which are used for a variety of applications. One of its applications is Customer Churn Prediction (CCP). Customer churn (or attrition) is the tendency of customers to stop using a company's products or services. It is important to predict churn where businesses can proactively target the customers, who are at high risk of leaving and create marketing campaigns to retain them. This study aims to build a predictive model to predict customer churn for Internet Service Providers (ISPs). Several experiments have been conducted on a dataset obtained from a Libyan ISP company to train the models. The dataset distribution was imbalanced, with only 5% of customers churned. To mitigate this, various oversampling techniques were used. In the proposed system, five diverse classifiers were used. Namely, Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) tree algorithm, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithms due to their relevance in this predictive context. The experimental findings showed that the XGBoost tree model yielded the most favorable outcomes, achieving an AUC value of 94%.

articleTitle: Virtual Smart Mirror as a Personal Trainer using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: People often struggle to maintain a consistent workout routine due to a lack of motivation, accountability, and guidance. Traditional personal trainers can be expensive and may not fit into everyone's schedule. Additionally, people may not feel comfortable working out in public spaces or gyms. This paper presents the development of Smart Mirror as a personal trainer that uses artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to create flexible and affordable solutions for individuals seeking guidance, motivation and personal workout plans. The smart mirror is aimed to act as a virtual personal trainer that provides real-time feedback and guidance during the workout, enhancing the overall performance and user experience. In this research work, computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms work in synergy to build interactive design that can eliminate the need for a traditional personal trainer. System efficacy is proved via real-time experiments where individuals' engagement is empowered in home workouts with accuracy.

articleTitle: Imaging Histopathology of Breast Cancer for Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common type of cancer seen in women globally, accounting for the majority of cancer-related fatalities in this population. Breast cancer is a serious global health problem. The most common subtype of breast cancer is invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), which accounts for around 80% of all instances of the disease that are detected. Efficient and accurate diagnosis of this illness is essential for choosing the best course of therapy and improving the prognosis of those who are afflicted. In this study, we present a reliable diagnosis tool based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN s) to improve patient survival rates by increasing the number of patients diagnosed early. The process of doing this usually involves the reuse of pre-trained CNN model pieces in a new CNN model through a process known as transfer learning. This approach is employed because a pre-trained CNN already knows how to extract useful and insightful features from a large collection of pictures, and fine-tuning a CNN via transfer learning is frequently quicker and simpler than building and training a new CNN network from the ground up. In this study, we re-trained three pre-trained CNNs (EffecientNet V2, Inception, and Xception) using a fresh dataset of IDC and Non-IDC pictures. By employing the EffecientNet V2 model, we were able to achieve a prediction accuracy of up to 99.56%.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on The Performance of Solar Cooker (Medium Size) Under Derna City Climate Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Energy consumption is increasing as a result of industrialization and population growth. It continues on to explain that new technologies for renewable energy, including solar energy, are being developed to fulfill this growing demand. It also highlights the parabolic solar cooker as one of the primary varieties of solar cookers, highlighting its capacity to quickly boil water and cook food at high temperatures. The cooker opto-thermal ratio (COR) is a performance measure based on the Hottel-Willier-Bliss (HWB) equation, which can be determined using the paper's recommended experimental single-step test. This concentrator cooker was constructed from several components, including steel, aluminum foil, and an outdated satellite dish. The concentrator solar cooker has the following specifications: 1.45 m, 1.65 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 0.202 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 0.657 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, rim angle, concentration ratio, surface area of the pot, depth of the parabola, focal length, and 59.05°, respectively. The thermal performance analysis of the concentrator cooker was evaluated by calculating the cooker opto-thermal ratio (COR). The cooker opto-thermal ratio and maximum achievable fluid temp were 0.18 and 208°C, respectively. The Parabolic solar cooker helps reduce food preparation energy costs because it consumes no energy. Thus, developing countries like Libya can greatly benefit from parabolic solar cookers.

articleTitle: Improving Block Matching and 3 Dimensions (BM3D) Filtering for Image Noise Removal Using Discrete Wavelet Transformation (DWT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: In the field of image denoising, Block Matching 3 Dimensions technique (BM3D) stated as a powerful technique that works to remove white Gaussian noise (A WGN). Despite BM3D shows its great success in comparison with the best denoising methods, still its visual quality decreases as the noise density escalates in noisy digital images. Therefore, the need to create a powerful image denoising method is necessary to accomplish the processing of image enhancement applications. The proposed method is introduced by. In this study, discrete wavelet transformation is applied on the LL level of the wavelet decomposition due to its ability to keep the smallest change in the original image. Furthermore, the coefficients of LL will be then divided to small blocks that contain contaminated pixels that suffer from additive white Gaussian noise (A WGN). Comparing with conventional block matching 3D (BM3D) that works well only on the similar patches, our proposed method has the ability to work on similar and dissimilar patches in order to find the inter and intra- correlations between dissimilar pixels. The proposed technique is examined on several digital benchmark images with different noise levels in terms of the quantity of the lost in the original and resulted pixels. In this regard, the performance of the tested images is estimated and then compared proposed with several high quality noise removal techniques according to several assessments such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and the figure of merits (FOM). The high amount of these factors reflects the success of the proposed technique. Further, it is interesting to observe the improvement in the running time where it was far less than the investigated noise removal algorithms.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation Generative Model for Segmenting 3D MRI Pediatric Brain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The segmentation of pediatric brain MRI into distinct tissues is important for the evaluation of pediatric brain development and the diagnosis of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders. However, when the used dataset diverges due to various acquisition protocols or biases among patient cohorts, existing deep learning algorithms cannot guarantee correct predictions. Unsupervised domain adaptation approaches have lately shown enormous potential for addressing this problem by limiting the divergence between the distributions of the used datasets. In this paper, we firstly developed a model called 3DUDRSeg, a 3D encoder-decoder for precise autonomous segmentation of pediatric brain tissues. Our proposed 3DUDRSeg model achieved a 98.88% DSC accuracy rate because of the employment of denes blocks and residual units that help relieve the degradation problem during training the network, allowing the performance advantages to be fully utilized. With this approach, our 3DUDRSeg can create more strong features to deal with the wide range of brain tissue variations. Then, we present 3DAdGanSeg, an entropy-based unsupervised domain adaptation framework for segmenting pediatric brain tissues in unannotated datasets via adversarial learning. The suggested model significantly influences the capability to distinguish the borders between tissue classes, with DSC of 85% and HD95 of 1.479 in the case of the dHCP dataset as the source domain and DSC of 81 % and HD95 of 2.061 when using the Schizophrenia Bulletin 2008 dataset as a source domain.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Data Center Complete Load Model Construction & Power Quality Assessment at Distribution Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper presents a major power quality indices assessment and evaluation of a validated three phase and single phase combined load models of a typical telecommunication data center electrical distribution network under several loading conditions, based on computer simulation. Typically, such networks are heavily penetrated by nonlinear loads which makes it a productive environment for generating distorted harmonic currents that can cause interruption to such data center operations. The built full network simulation model using Matlab/Simulink computer program is utilized to emulate various network loading states (light, moderate and heavy) to be evaluated and investigated according to the IEEE519-2014 standards. The major power quality guides investigated involve the network lines current total harmonic distortion THDi%, network nodes (busbars) voltage THDv% and total true line power factor (T.P.F) at each connection point. AI-Madar AI-Jadid telecommunication Company data center electrical distribution network is the case study considered.

articleTitle: Exploring Knowledge Landscapes: Clustering and Topic Modeling of Sebha University Scientific Publications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: The continuous and exponential growth in scientific publications poses a challenge in manually sorting and searching for specific topics within a university's publications. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and clustering methods, particularly the K-Means, have shown satisfactory performance in handling large volumes of textual data. Furthermore, topic modeling methods, notably praised for their effectiveness in organizing textual documents. This study focuses on evaluating the performance of the K-Means and Latent Dirichlet Allocation in clustering Sebha University scientific publications. Different term weighting is employed namely term frequency inverse document frequency, and Word2Vec to represent the tokens. K-Means demonstrated notable performance when coupled with Word2vec, as indicated by metrics such as the Davies-Bouldin Index, Silhouette Score, Calinski-Harabasz Index, and Inertia. The best performance was observed when using term frequency inverse document frequency with the Entropy metric. The evaluation metrics for K-Means did not unanimously agree on the optimal number of clusters. In contrast, Latent Dirichlet Allocation consistently performed well, with all measurements agreeing on the best results with the smallest number of clusters. Among the various combinations tested, Latent Dirichlet Allocation paired with Word2vec produced the best results across metrics, demonstrating superior cohesion strength through the topic coherence metric and minimizing noise aggregates based on the entropy metric.

articleTitle: A CNN -based Crosswalk Guidance for the Visually Impaired that Combines a Fuzzy Logic Controller and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a support system for visual impairments that combines computer vision techniques, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC), and Genetic Algorithms (GA). The proposed system combines the advantages of three intelligent logic systems: CNN, FLC, and GA. This integrated system, named the NFG (Neural Fuzzy Genetic) system, aims to detect and track objects, measure the distance between obstacles and the blind or visually impaired (BVI) person, and provide movement guidance using three ultrasonic sensors with FLC. The combination of these technologies provides a novel approach to improving the mobility and safety of individuals who are Blind or Visually Impaired (BVI). In particular, the use of object detection and tracking through CNN is implemented, with the range for obstacle detection extending up to 40 meters. The obstacle recognition system is trained on the ResNet50 model, comprising 50 million trained images and over 1000 classifications of obstacles, resulting in high accuracy in identifying obstacles. This speed in identifying, avoiding, and guiding ensures efficient navigation towards the intended destination. FLC is then utilized to provide guidance that considers uncertainty in the information used for guidance such as near, far. It assists in making appropriate decisions in the event of obstacles, navigating around them, and determining directions for movement in obstacle-free paths. The system moves at a steering angle determined by fuzzy rules. The information from CNNs and sensors with FLC is integrated to optimize guidance information using GA. This optimization process fine-tunes the rules of FLC, aiming to find the best possible solutions for effective guidance.

articleTitle: A Holistic Approach for Cyber Security Vulnerability Assessment Based on Open Source Tools: Nikto, Acunitx, ZAP, Nessus and Enhanced with AI-Powered Tool ImmuniWeb
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: This paper describes a cyber security vulnerability assessment methodology powered by AI tactics. The AI-powered tool “ImmuniWeb AI” effectively supported the tools of the suggested approach by automating a number of vulnerability management process tasks, including scanning, evaluation, prioritizing, and remediation. The recommended methodology makes use of the Nikto, Acunitx, Nessus, and ZAP proxy tools, which have been improved by the ImmuniWeb AI online tool, to quickly and effectively scan target systems in order to identify any vulnerabilities. Using such a variety of tools with a wide range of expertise practically produced a comprehensive method that can identify system vulnerabilities and generate well-written reports with appropriate remedy recommendations depending on the vulnerabilities' scores and level of danger. As a result, the outcomes showed how effective the suggested methodology.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Software Maintenance Approach Based on World-Class Manufacturing Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Software, while it is developed, grows in complexity and size, making its maintenance a major problem for software companies. This study aims to develop an approach to improve software maintenance to detect unexpected and common failures and reduce the time it takes to repair failures. The approach was applied to the IT sector using the World Class Manufacturing (WCM) approach and divided into four phases: During phase I, the project team and stakeholders held a brainstorming session to create a Standard Maintenance Procedure (SMP) document tool. During phase II, a Machine Ledger (ML) was used to investigate the failure. If the failure was not brand-new, the SMP document's instructions were followed, and a corrective maintenance procedure was performed. When a failure occurs for the first time in phase III, an Emergency Work Order (EWO) tool is used to analyze the breakdown and determine its primary cause. Phase IV involves recording the failure, to be fixed, and the amount of time it required. After determining the root cause of the problem and carrying out corrective maintenance, the data in the SMP document was updated. The approach was evaluated in a Digital Archive Company in Benghazi and a questionnaire was distributed via Google form to four different companies. The findings showed promising results and increased efficiency, demonstrating the importance of using the suggested approach for software maintenance.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Diabetes Using Binary Whale Optimization Algorithm-Based Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
abstract: Early diagnosis of diabetes is critical for prompt treatment that can prevent the disease's progression to potentially lethal complications. Due to factors such as high blood pressure, genetic diabetes, and modern lifestyles that include inactivity, diabetes is one of the most common and severe diseases in the world. Using machine learning to assist in the creation of quick and precise diagnoses is one endeavor being made in the health sector. Feature selection approaches are a crucial step towards achieving high classification accuracy since they improve the efficiency of learning algorithms. In order to detect diabetes disease, the features from the Pima Indians Diabetes (PID) dataset were selected using a binary whale optimization algorithm (BWOA). After that, the classification is applied by the Gaussian process classifier (GPC) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) independently. The proposed BWOA-GPC system obtained the highest classification accuracy of up to 85.94%.
